To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ensemble square root method of assimilation is more accurate than the standard Kalman filter method of assimilation for the same ensemble sizes, because it avoids sampling errors that are inherent in the perturbed observation method of assimilation.

(i) the EnSRF is a more accurate ensemble filter than the EnKF, (ii) the EnSRFs are more accurate than the ensemble transform Kalman filter (ETKF), and (iii) the EnSRFS are more accurate than EnSRF with perturbed observations (EnSRF-P).
the EnSRF has a smaller analysis-error covariance estimate than the EnKF, and that this difference can be explained by the fact that the EnSRFs estimate is not negatively biased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of ensemble data assimilation.
the use of ensemble methods in data assimilation, and the results presented here are relevant to the use of any ensemble Kalman filter.
the problem of how to estimate the analysis-error covariance in the ensemble Kalman filter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EnKF and the EnSRF are equivalent when perturbed observations are not used, and when the observations are processed one at the time.

the EnKF and EnSRF are equally accurate when they use the same ensemble size and the same number of perturbed observations, and that the EnSRF is more accurate for the same ensemble and observation size.
ensemble data assimilation schemes that do not use perturbed observations should be used when feasible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perturbation of observations is not needed to achieve accurate analysis-error covariance estimates in an ensemble data assimilation method.
ensemble Kalman filter methods are more accurate when perturbed observations are not used.
ensemble data assimilation schemes that use perturbed observation are not optimal and that the EnSRF is the most efficient of the ensemble filter schemes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ensemble filter methods can be implemented without perturbed observations.
the EnKF is a robust method that is not overly sensitive to the details of the ensemble update scheme.
the use of perturbed observations in an ensemble filter is not necessary to obtain a positive impact from ensemble data assimilation.
